description.summary: which workspace (realm) a desktop group belongs to

protocol.description: The compositor keeps one set of desktops per Kora workspace, and announces every one of them through ext_workspace_v1 as its own group. Nothing there says which workspace a group belongs to; this protocol does, so a switcher can lay desktops out under the workspace that owns them.

interface.name: kora_workspace_realm_manager_v1
interface.description:
Binding this global announces the workspace of every desktop group the client can see, and of every group announced afterwards.
From version 2 a machine-plane client may also put a layer surface of its own into a workspace, so it is shown, focusable and capturable only while that workspace is on screen — the way a workspace's own windows are. A client inside a workspace has its layer surfaces there already.

entry.name: not_permitted
entry.summary: the client is inside a workspace; its surfaces are already scoped to it

request.name: destroy
request.description: Informs the server that the client will no longer use this global.

event.name: realm

description.summary: the workspace a group belongs to

event.description: The desktops in `group` belong to the Kora workspace `id`, the same identifier the workspace registry uses. Sent once per group, after the group itself has been announced.

request.name: assign

description.summary: put a layer surface in a workspace

request.description:
The layer surface backed by `surface` belongs to the Kora workspace `id` from now on: the compositor renders it, hit-tests it and captures it only while that workspace is on screen. Assigning again moves it; destroying the surface forgets it.
Only a client outside every workspace may ask. One inside a workspace gets the not_permitted error: its layer surfaces are scoped to its own workspace by the compositor, and it cannot put one anywhere else.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: a wl_surface with a layer surface role
